The '''Gulfstream G280''' is a twin-engine [[business jet]] built by [[Israel Aerospace Industries]] (IAI) for [[Gulfstream Aerospace]]. It began delivery to users in 2012.

==Development==
[[File:4X-CVC Udi Brill.jpg|thumb|G280 in flight before painting]]

In 2005, Gulfstream and IAI began designing a follow-on aircraft to the [[Gulfstream G200]]. The new model, named ''G250'', was launched in 2008. Planned improvements included new glass cockpit and engines, larger wing, and heated leading edges.<ref name="FI Oct 2008">{{cite news |url= https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/nbaa-2008-g-force-g250-targets-the-largest-cabin-an-316915/ |title= G FORCE G250 targets the largest cabin and longest |work= Flight International |date= October 5, 2008}}; {{cite news |url= https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/nbaa-2008-pictures-gulfstream-launches-g250-set-t-316761/ |title= Gulfstream launches G250 set to dominate super mid-size sector from 2011 |work= Flight International |date= October 5, 2008}}</ref>

The G250 took its [[maiden flight]] on December 11, 2009, in Tel Aviv, Israel.<ref>{{cite news |url= https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/pictures-video-gulfstream-g250-performs-first-fli-336090/ |title= Gulfstream G250 performs first flight successfully |work= Flight global |date= December 11, 2009}}</ref> In July 2011, the G250 was renamed ''G280'', as the company had "determined that G280 is a more amenable number sequence [than G250] in certain cultures."<ref>{{cite press release |url= http://gulfstreamnews.com/news/gulfstream-renames-g250 |title= Gulfstream renames G250 |publisher= Gulfstream |date= July 18, 2011 |access-date= October 27, 2016 |archive-date= December 15, 2018 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20181215225151/https://www.gulfstreamnews.com/news/gulfstream-renames-g250 |url-status= dead }}</ref> In Mandarin, the number 250 can be translated as "stupid" or "idiotic".<ref>{{cite news |url= https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/gulfstream-rebrands-its-g250-the-g280-359645/ |title= Gulfstream rebrands its G250 the G280 |work= Flight Global |date= 19 July 2011}}</ref>

After the flight test program, the G280 demonstrated a range of {{convert|3,600|nmi|km|abbr=on}} at Mach 0.80 with four passengers and NBAA IFR reserves in 2011. It can fly from London to New York or Singapore to Dubai. Its balanced field length has been reduced to {{convert|4,750|ft|m}} from the G200's {{convert|4,960|ft|m}}.<ref>{{cite press release |url= http://gulfstreamnews.com/news/gulfstream-demonstrates-improved-performance-for-g280 |title= Gulfstream Demonstrates Improved Performance For G280 |date= October 9, 2011 |publisher= Gulfstream Aerospace |access-date= March 21, 2014 |archive-date= December 15, 2018 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20181215225033/https://www.gulfstreamnews.com/news/gulfstream-demonstrates-improved-performance-for-g280 |url-status= dead }}</ref>

The G280 was provisionally certified in December 2011 by Israel.<ref name=FG_full_cert/> In July 2012, the US [[Federal Aviation Administration|FAA]] released a report with conditions to ensure no security gaps in the G280's electronic systems.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/FR-2012-06-28/html/2012-15913.htm |title= FAA Warns of Gulfstream Electronic Security Gap |publisher=GPO.gov |date= June 28, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release |url= http://gulfstreamnews.com/news/gulfstream-g280-poised-for-certification |title= Gulfstream G280 Poised for Certification |publisher= Gulfstream |date= August 15, 2012 |access-date= October 27, 2016 |archive-date= October 28, 2016 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20161028020103/http://gulfstreamnews.com/news/gulfstream-g280-poised-for-certification |url-status= dead }}</ref> It received full certification from Israel and the US on September 4, 2012.<ref name=FG_full_cert>{{cite news |author= Sarsfield, Kate |url= http://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/israel-and-usa-grant-full-certification-for-gulfstream-g280-376053 |title= Israel and USA grant full certification for Gulfstream G280 |work= Flight International |date= September 4, 2012}}</ref>
In 2021, its equipped price was $24.5M.<ref>{{cite news |url= https://infogram.com/bca-table-jets-1h8n6m3l3dvqj4x?live |title= Purchase planning handbook - Jets table |date= Second Quarter 2021 |work= Business & Commercial Aircraft}}</ref>

Gulfstream unveiled the '''G300''', an updated version of the G280, on 30 September, 2025. The updated aircraft flew for the first time on December 5, 2025.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Trautvetter |first1=Chad |title=Gulfstream Finally Takes Wraps Off Super-midsize G300 |url=http://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2025-09-30/gulfstream-finally-takes-wraps-super-midsize-g300 |access-date=2 October 2025 |work=AIN |date=30 September 2025}}</ref>

==Design==
The aerodynamic design of its wing and [[empennage]], and design of the interior were performed by Gulfstream; detailed design was performed by IAI to Gulfstream's requirements.<ref name="FG NBAA 2008">{{cite news |url= https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/nbaa-2008-gulfstream-know-how-buoys-g250-performanc-316880/ |title= NBAA 2008: Gulfstream know-how buoys G250 performance claims |work= Flight International |date= October 5, 2008}}</ref>  It is a Gulfstream designed aircraft under a new type certificate.<ref>[http://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/aviation-international-news/2012-10-02/gulfstream-scores-double-win-g280-g650-certification "Gulfstream Scores Double Win with G280, G650 Certification"]. AIN Online, October 2012.</ref>

[[File:Gulfstream G280 cabin interior with divan.JPG|thumb|G280 cabin]]
The aircraft has several improvements, among them increased cabin length (external fuselage dimensions remain unchanged; the rear fuselage fuel tank was eliminated to add {{convert|17|in|cm}} of usable interior area).<ref name=Flying_G280>{{cite news |url= http://aviationweek.com/awin/flying-gulfstream-g280 |title= Flying the Gulfstream G280 |work= Aviation Week & Space Technology |date= October 29, 2012}}</ref> It has a new [[Honeywell HTF7000|HTF7250G]] engine, new T-tail (with larger horizontal and vertical stabilizers), wing anti-ice provided by engine bleed air, cabin with four more windows and access from the cabin to the baggage compartment. It competes against the [[Bombardier Challenger 300]] and the [[Cessna Citation X]]+. The fuselage, empennage and [[landing gear]] are manufactured by IAI, the wing by [[Spirit AeroSystems]] (now by [[Triumph Group]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/spirit-aerosystems-to-transfer-tulsa-okla-wing-business-to-triumph-group-1418133280|title=Spirit AeroSystems to Transfer Tulsa Wing Business to Triumph Group|last1=Dulaney|first1=Chelsey|date=2014-12-09|last2=Ostrower|first2=Jon|newspaper=Wall Street Journal|issn=0099-9660|access-date=2016-12-20}}</ref>), and the aircraft is assembled in Israel. It is then ferried to Dallas, Texas, for interior finishing and painting.<ref name="FI Oct 2008"/><ref name="FG NBAA 2008"/><ref name=Flying_G280/>

Its wing is a new design, using the [[Gulfstream G550]] airfoil, and has a larger area of 495 ft<sup>2</sup> vs. 369 ft<sup>2</sup> of the G200. This allows the business jet to climb directly to {{cvt|43000|ft|m}}. Design cruise for the new airfoil is Mach 0.80, vs. Mach 0.75 for the G200 wing.<ref name=Flying_G280/> Flying at an altitude of {{cvt|41000|ft|m}} and Mach 0.82 ({{cvt|467|knots|km/h|disp=or}}), each engine burns {{cvt|900|lb}} of fuel per hour.<ref>{{cite news |author=Matt Thurber |date=February 9, 2018 |title=Pilot Report : Gulfstream G280 |url=https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2018-02-09/pilot-report-gulfstream-g280 |magazine=Aviation International News}}</ref>
